service.name: Last Consulate
service.serviceType: Instrumental downtempo music for cocktail hours, dinners and corporate receptions
service.description: Last Consulate, one musician on upright bass and guitar over downtempo electronics, playing original instrumental music with jazz improvisation at conversation volume for arrival, cocktails and dinner at corporate events, galas and private dinners across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.a: Original instrumental music: upright bass and guitar out front, over downtempo electronics with slow hip-hop drums, worn keys and delayed guitars, with jazz improvisation on top. It sounds closer to an early-2000s downtempo record than to a jazz set, there are no covers and no singer, and the bass line is usually the melody.

It plays arrival, cocktails and dinner at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, so your guests talk across it the whole time. It isn't a playlist, though: the bass lines are improvised on the night, and the loops hold the tempo in the slow band all evening, so the music never drifts up as the venue fills.

One musician and one rig. It sets up in 6 by 4 feet on one dedicated 20-amp circuit, loads in inside 45 minutes, and plays through its own small sound system or the venue's house system, whichever the space wants.

Client dinners and member events where the conversation is the point, the doors and the dinner at a gala, the welcome evening of a corporate retreat, a cocktail reception in a hotel lobby, and dinner parties at home. Anywhere the music should feel like a late jazz set or a hotel lobby rather than a band.

faqs.q: Can it carry a whole evening?
faqs.a: Arrival through dinner, yes. When the night wants a floor afterward, a band or the DJ takes over on the same contract and the same sound system, so Last Consulate is the first half of one booking rather than a separate vendor.
